memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "In this way he will make atonement for the Most Holy Place because of the uncleanness and rebellion of the Israelites, whatever their sins have been. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which is among them in the midst of their uncleanness." - Lev 16:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is something we might not expect: the tabernacle itself needed atonement.

Not just the people. The building. The furniture. The holiest room in Israel. Why? Because it stood in the midst of their uncleanness. God's dwelling place was located in the middle of a sinful camp, and the sin of the people affected even the place where He met with them.

This is worth sitting with. Sin is never a private matter. It touches what surrounds it. A family's atmosphere carries what its members bring into it. A workplace takes on the character of the people in it. A church is shaped by what the congregation lives out through the week.

And notice the phrase whatever their sins have been. God does not need a catalogue. He is not waiting for a full disclosure before He can act. The blood covers what was named and what was not.

But hold on to the wonder of it. God did not move out. Faced with a camp full of uncleanness, He stayed — and made provision so He could keep dwelling among them.

He has not moved out on you either.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How has your sin affected the atmosphere around you?
2. What comfort is there in the phrase "whatever their sins have been"?
3. What does it mean that God chooses to dwell in the midst of imperfect people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You do not withdraw from Your people but make a way to stay. Cleanse not only me but the places I influence, and dwell among us. Amen.
